title: An arbitrarily large wire reversal costs at most two Gaussian contractions
summary: A concrete example of treating many interactions collectively. It suggests studying permutation sign functions and compact correction dictionaries for tensor contraction or circuit simulation.
content: For b reversed wires with occupation weight w, the ordinary-versus-fermionic correction is (-1)^(w(w-1)/2)=((1-i)/2)i^w+((1+i)/2)(-i)^w. Both terms factor into unary weights, which preserve Gaussian tensors through diagonal matrix scaling. Thus all b(b-1)/2 crossings of a reversal require at most two Gaussian contractions, independent of b; a fixed total parity needs only one term.
whenToUse: A concrete example of treating many interactions collectively. It suggests studying permutation sign functions and compact correction dictionaries for tensor contraction or circuit simulation.
limitations: Odd characteristic and a square root of -1 are required for this displayed formula. General permutations need not be cheap: d disjoint adjacent swaps require 2^d terms in the unary-product correction dictionary by Walsh matrix rank. That lower bound does not cover entangled Gaussian corrections.
